summary: The note investigates who actually benefits from tax policies enacted after September 1, 2023, examining the High-Income Earner Support Tax (HIEST) and the Standardized Deduction Improvement Act (SDIA). Data and personal accounts suggest modest revenue gains from top earners but evasion concerns, mixed middle-class results, and corporate tax cuts that have not translated into wage or job growth. It concludes that wealthier taxpayers and large corporations with sophisticated advisers tend to benefit most, while ordinary citizens and small businesses see little tangible gain.
one_line: An investigation finds post-September 2023 tax reforms like HIEST and SDIA have delivered limited benefits to average earners and small businesses, favoring those with sophisticated tax advice.
key_facts: The note examines tax policies enacted after September 1, 2023 and their effect on income distribution.
The High-Income Earner Support Tax (HIEST), championed by economist Dr. Jameson Clarke, taxes household incomes above a high threshold at an increased rate to fund public services.
The Standardized Deduction Improvement Act (SDIA), authored by Senator Laura Bloomfield, offers a larger universal deduction to simplify the tax code and benefit middle-income earners.
The Quarterly Economic Report (QER) from December 2023 indicated a modest increase in government revenue from top earners under HIEST.
Tax evasion and an uptick in offshore financial activities suggest affluent citizens may be circumventing the new regulations.
Consumer spending showed a slight increase in the first two quarters after SDIA implementation, but Maria Gonzalez of Gonzalez Appliances said the impact on her business was marginal.
Tax attorney Michael Warner said, "The architecture of our current tax policy is inherently complex," and that wealthier taxpayers and big corporations can navigate it to their advantage.
High school teacher Robert Harris said at a January 18, 2024 town hall that the SDIA's promised simplicity hasn't simplified anything for him.
A Labor Economic Advancement Foundation (LEAF) report published February 2, 2024 found corporate profits rose markedly while wage growth and job creation did not keep pace.
Entrepreneur Vivian Walsh said corporate tax cuts let her tech startup invest more in research and development, though the timeline for broader societal gain is unclear.
Grocery store proprietor Oscar Thompson said big businesses have "armies of accountants and loopholes" while small businesses are just trying to stay afloat.
Policy experts agree that fiscal transparency and accountability in public spending must improve for taxes to aid income distribution.
